articles.title: Ala do STF vê Lei da Dosimetria como alternativa à revisão criminal  de Bolsonaro  | G1
articles.standfirst: Ideia é que o tribunal analise, após a eleição, as ações que questionam lei aprovada no Congresso. Texto prevê a redução de penas para condenados por atentados golpistas no país.
articles.summary: Ideia é que o tribunal analise, após a eleição, as ações que questionam lei aprovada no Congresso. Texto prevê a redução de penas para condenados por atentados golpistas no país.
articles.body:
Uma ala do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) defende julgar após as eleições as ações que questionam a chamada Lei da Dosimetria, que prevê a redução de penas para condenados por atentados golpistas no país.

A análise da norma é apontada como uma possível alternativa para o julgamento de pedidos de revisão criminal do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro , que buscam anular a condenação a 27 anos e três meses de prisão na trama golpista.

Segundo esses ministros ouvidos pela TV Globo , a dosimetria é um caminho alternativo à revisão criminal porque ela, na prática, diminuiria o tempo de cumprimento da pena de Bolsonaro, aliados e condenados pelos ataques de 8 de janeiro, sem necessariamente criar um novo embate na Corte.

De acordo com essas avaliações, haveria maioria na Corte para manter a dosimetria, com eventuais propostas de ajustes.

Já a anulação pela revisão criminal seria mais difícil de construir. Chegar a uma maioria no atual cenário da Corte seria mais complicado, já que haveria necessidade de derrubar o entendimento fixado pela Primeira Turma, que condenou os réus na trama golpista.

🔎A norma alterou dispositivos da Lei de Execução Penal e do Código Penal para estabelecer novos critérios de progressão de regime e remição de pena em condenações por crimes contra o Estado Democrático de Direito.

Segundo cálculos da defesa de Bolsonaro, com a mudança, a pena seria reduzida entre 2 anos e 5 meses a 3 anos . Durante a discussão da mudança no Congresso, parte dos ministros do Supremo indicou que a medida poderia ser acolhida pela Corte, enquanto uma anistia seria derrubada.

Relator, o ministro Alexandre de Moraes suspendeu em maio a aplicação da norma até que o plenário analise ações que questionam a validade da regra — Foto: Rosinei Coutinho/STF

A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) se manifestou, em junho, contra a suspensão da lei , porque de forma provisória não identificou, naquele momento, desvio de finalidade por eventual construção da lei para beneficiar condenados pelo 8 de janeiro.

Com o parecer da PRG, o caso já pode ser levado para julgamento no plenário. Isso depende, no entanto, da liberação pelo relator. Depois, o presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, precisa marcar uma data para o julgamento, caso ocorra no plenário presencial.

O ministro Kassio Nunes Marques é o relator dos pedidos de revisão criminal apresentados por Jair Bolsonaro — Foto: Rosinei Coutinho/STF

A interlocutores, Nunes Marques tem afirmado que é preciso enfrentar o tema. Uma das ações ainda depende de parecer da PGR para poder ser julgada.

🔎 A revisão criminal é uma ação que permite contestar uma condenação que já se tornou definitiva, em situações previstas em lei, como diante do surgimento de novas provas. A medida não representa um novo julgamento e é considerada excepcional.

O objetivo do instrumento é corrigir erros judiciários e exige a apresentação de novos elementos de provas que possam comprovar a inocência como:

comprovar que a sentença foi contrária à lei penal ou às provas do processo;

comprovar que a sentença que se baseou em depoimentos, exames ou documentos falsos.

O novo pedido da chamada revisão criminal foi apresentado na semana passada com base em novos argumentos , como um parecer técnico que teria identificado problemas na cadeia de custódia de provas (mecanismos para proteger o material) e limitações para verificar parte das provas digitais utilizadas no processo.

Também há menções à crise do caso Master, como declarações do ministro Alexandre de Moraes sobre o conteúdo do celular de Daniel Vorcaro.

A Procuradoria vai avaliar se as questões levantadas pela defesa justificam ou não uma reavaliação do caso.

articles.title: TSE suspende propaganda de Lula sobre Flávio Bolsonaro e caso Master | G1
articles.standfirst: Conteúdo também afirma que Alfredo Gaspar é investigado por estupro. Pedido de abertura de investigação contra o candidato a vice na chapa foi rejeitado por falta de elementos para embasar a denúncia.
articles.summary: O TSE suspendeu a propaganda de Lula que associava Flávio Bolsonaro ao caso Master e Alfredo Gaspar a um crime de estupro arquivado por falta de provas.
articles.body:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) determinou a suspensão imediata de uma propaganda eleitoral veiculada pela campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) que diz que Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) é investigado por corrupção e lavagem de dinheiro no caso do Banco Master.

o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vão disputar o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais no próximo dia 25 de outubro.

🔎Flávio é investigado pela Polícia Federal (PF) em inquérito aberto para apurar a possível prática de crimes relacionados ao financiamento por Daniel Vorcaro, dono do Master, na produção do filme "Dark Horse", sobre a trajetória do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (entenda mais abaixo).

O conteúdo também afirma que o vice de Flávio, Alfredo Gaspar, é alvo de investigação por estupro de vulnerável. O pedido de abertura de investigação foi arquivado por falta de elementos para embasar a denúncia.

Na decisão, o presidente do TSE, ministro Nunes Marques, afirma que a propaganda traz "imputações criminais desprovidas de lastro mínimo, em espaço de comunicação de alcance nacional e custeado pela sociedade".

"Admitir o uso do horário eleitoral gratuito para esse fim significaria converter instrumento concebido para assegurar a igualdade de oportunidades entre os competidores em meio de desequilíbrio da própria disputa", diz o ministro.

Segundo a decisão, a PF investiga suspeitas de lavagem de dinheiro, evasão de divisas, corrupção e outros possíveis crimes que teriam sido praticados, em tese, por Flávio Bolsonaro no contexto do financiamento do filme junto a Daniel Vorcaro, dono do extinto Banco Master.

➡️A Polícia Federal recebeu um pedido para abrir um inquérito contra Alfredo Gaspar, após suspeitas de estupro de vulnerável envolvendo a senadora Soraya Thronicke e o deputado Lindbergh Farias. O ministro Gilmar Mendes, do STF, determinou o arquivamento da apuração por falta de elementos para embasar a denúncia.

A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) já havia manifestado por rejeitar o pedido de abertura de inquérito.

🎥 O filme "Dark Horse" ganhou notoriedade após a divulgação, pelo site Intercept Brasil, de conversas entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Daniel Vorcaro, em que o filho do ex-presidente solicita recursos para financiar a produção cinematográfica.

O banqueiro ajudou a financiar o filme, e as negociações envolveram contatos diretos com o filho mais velho do ex-presidente, que pediu dinheiro e pressionava pelos pagamentos.

Vorcaro chegou a pagar R$ 61 milhões aos produtores do filme, via fundo nos Estados Unidos.

Ao todo, Flávio Bolsonaro teria negociado o repasse de US$ 24 milhões, cerca de R$ 134 milhões na época, para financiar a produção.

R$ 75,1 milhões - valor que a produtora diz ter gasto;

R$ 61 milhões - valor que Daniel Vorcaro teria destinado ao filme via fundo nos EUA;

R$ 134 milhões - valor que Flávio Bolsonaro teria negociado antes de Vorcaro ser preso;

R$ 108 milhões - valor do contrato entre ONG de Karina da Gama e a Prefeitura de SP para instalação de wi-fi na capital paulista.

articles.title: Mãe arrecada brinquedos em homenagem ao filho que morreu aos 3 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Além dos brinquedos para o Dia das Crianças, a moradora de Presidente Prudente (SP), Maiara Lourenção, está preparando uma ação social no dia 18 de outubro, data em que Pedro completaria quatro anos.
articles.summary: Como forma de ressignificar o luto, uma mãe de Presidente Prudente (SP) arrecadou mais de 700 brinquedos em homenagem ao filho de três anos, que morreu em março deste ano.
articles.body:
Como forma de ressignificar o luto pela morte do filho, uma mãe de Presidente Prudente (SP) arrecadou mais de 700 brinquedos para serem doados a entidades sociais que atendem crianças. A campanha foi realizada em celebração ao Dia das Crianças e também como uma homenagem a Pedro, filho caçula de Maiara Lourenção, de 37 anos, que morreu aos três anos, em março deste ano.

Ao g1 , a publicitária e servidora municipal contou que decidiu organizar a campanha por conta própria e transformar a dor da perda em uma ação voltada a outras crianças. A ideia foi arrecadar os brinquedos e destiná-los a instituições sociais infantis.

“O Pedro sempre foi uma criança muito fácil de lidar. Ele era expansivo, falante, alegre, parecia pertencer a todos os lugares, era meu grande parceiro.”

Mãe arrecada brinquedos em homenagem ao filho que morreu aos 3 anos em Presidente Prudente (SP) — Foto: Maiara Lourenção/Arquivo pessoal

“Conversando com a minha mãe, achamos que seria uma boa maneira de devolver ao mundo o amor e a alegria dele por meio da doação de brinquedos para crianças que talvez não tivessem a oportunidade de ganhar um”, continua.

Foi a partir da ideia da família que, ao longo das semanas, os moradores arrecadaram centenas de brinquedos, que foram distribuídos para cinco instituições: Creche Municipal Dr. Aziz Felipe, a ala pediátrica do Hospital Regional (HR), o Hospital Esperança (HE), a Associação dos Cegos de Presidente Prudente e a Escola de Educação Especial Lumen.

Além dos brinquedos, Maiara afirma estar preparando uma ação social para o dia 18 de outubro, data em que Pedro completaria quatro anos.

“A nossa intenção é fazer o movimento anualmente, sempre no Dia das Crianças, para celebrar também o aniversário dele, que seria no dia 18 de outubro.”

A programação da primeira edição do evento vai contar com brinquedos infláveis, distribuição de alimentos como sorvete, suco, pipoca e algodão-doce. O evento será aberto à comunidade, na Praça CEU “Professor Samoel Brondi”, das 9h às 12h. Neste dia, não ocorrerá a entrega de brinquedos.

A praça fica na Avenida Tancredo Neves, 2.150, no bairro Parque Alvorada, em Presidente Prudente.

Segundo a servidora pública, o Dia das Crianças foi criado para celebrar a infância, o brincar e, por meio do brinquedo, a criança tem a oportunidade de desenvolvimento físico, emocional e social.

“Nada mais justo que proporcionar essa experiência para algumas das crianças da nossa cidade. Acho que podemos criar muitas memórias por meio desse dia.”

Maiara reforça que a mensagem que pretende passar com essa atitude “é de que podemos transformar a saudade e a dor em coisas boas e solidariedade.”

“Que cada brinquedo entregue carregue um pouco do amor do Pedro e faça sua memória permanecer viva através de outras crianças.”

Aos pais que também estejam passando pelo luto de perder um filho, a mãe do Pedro e do Vicente reforça que não há palavras para descrever ou que possam aliviar a saudade.

Os dois filhos de Maiara: Vicente, de 8 anos (à esq.), e Pedro, de 3 anos (à dir.) — Foto: Maiara Lourenção/Arquivo pessoal

“Eu também estou aprendendo, todos os dias, a conviver com a ausência do meu filho Pedro e com um amor que continua tão grande quanto antes. Sei que existem dias em que simplesmente levantar e seguir em frente já é uma grande vitória.”

“Não precisamos fingir que está tudo bem. Podemos sentir saudade, chorar, lembrar, falar dos nossos filhos e, ao mesmo tempo, encontrar pequenos motivos para continuar”, completa.

articles.title: DF terá bancada 100% feminina e conservadora no Senado; veja perfis | G1
articles.standfirst: Bia Kicis e Michelle Bolsonaro, ambas do PL, se juntam à senadora Damares Alves (Republicanos), eleita em 2022. As três se denominam conservadoras e defensoras da família tradicional.
articles.summary: Michelle Bolsonaro e Bia Kicis se juntam a Damares Alves na bancada feminina do DF no Senado, formando um trio de parlamentares conservadoras e defensoras da família.
articles.body:
A partir de 2027, o Distrito Federal será a primeira unidade da Federação a ser totalmente representada por mulheres no Senado.

Eleitas no último fim de semana, as novas senadoras Michelle Bolsonaro ( PL ) e Bia Kicis (PL) tomam posse em fevereiro – e se juntam na bancada à senadora Damares Alves (Republicanos), eleita em 2022 e com mandato até 2031.

➡️ O DF é, atualmente, governado por uma mulher. Celina Leão ( PP ) era vice e assumiu o governo em março, com a renúncia de Ibaneis Rocha (MDB). Ela disputa o segundo turno contra Leandro Grass ( PT ) – a votação será no dia 25.

A presença de mulheres na nominata fez parte da estratégia de campanha de Bia e Michelle – e de Celina Leão, aliada de ambas.

Celina afirmou "querer muito ter duas mulheres no Senado". Um desejo, aliás, que não excluía as outros nomes competitivos fortes na disputa na capital. Leila do Vôlei ( PDT ) teve 21,25% e Erika Kokay (PT), 18,91% dos votos – ficaram em 3º e 4º na disputa pelas duas vagas.

Para a cientista política e professora da Universidade de Brasília (UnB) Flávia Biroli, uma contradição chama atenção: nenhuma mulher foi eleita para as oito vagas do DF na Câmara dos Deputados.

"A eleição do DF para o Senado acabou não sendo a regra, está mais para a exceção. Na Câmara, embora tenha a maior bancada, o PL está abaixo do PT no número de mulheres", compara.

Damares Alves, Bia Kicis e Michelle Bolsonaro, em evento de campanha no DF — Foto: Instagram/Reprodução

Por um lado, a bancada 100% feminina é uma conquista para a representação feminina na política. Por outro, as mulheres que vão integrar essa bancada se notabilizaram por criticar movimentos feministas – e, vez ou outra, por votar contra projetos que beneficiavam mulheres.

Em 2023, como deputada federal, Bia Kicis foi uma das 10 parlamentares que votaram contra o projeto de lei que tenta assegurar a igualdade salarial entre homens e mulheres .

Na ocasião, a parlamentar afirmou que a igualdade já era prevista na CLT e que era contra "impor multa pesada a quem emprega mulheres e homens".

Estreante em mandatos eletivos, Michelle Bolsonaro chefiou o PL Mulher por três anos, sempre com a meta de ampliar a participação das mulheres no partido.

Em discursos a filiadas, a ex-primeira-dama chegou a falar que apoiava uma política “feminina, não feminista". Disse, também, ser u ma mulher "ajudadora do esposo". E defendeu uma "submissão saudável".

"Não estamos aqui para demonizar a figura masculina. Quem faz isso, com muita propriedade, são as feministas, as parlamentares de esquerda, do PT, do PSOL”, afirmou na ocasião. Michelle disse ainda, em outro discurso, que iria orar para que essas mulheres se convertessem.

Para Biroli, o resultado do primeiro turno está ligado mais à projeção das candidaturas de direita e extrema-direita que ao avanço da pauta de representatividade.

"Me parece que há uma retórica conservadora que coloca a família no centro das preocupações, associadas à defesa de uma ordem social e política conservadora. Na conjuntura eleitoral, isso se associa ao antipetismo e à crítica ao STF. No caso de direitos das mulheres, especificamente, elas representam mulheres 'empoderadas'. São poderosas, sem dúvida, e nesse sentido oferecem imagens de mulheres fortalecidas. Mas não se posicionam em favor de direitos individuais das mulheres ou do fortalecimento de políticas públicas e responsabilidade estatal para com as mulheres", afirma.

A cientista política ressalta que é importante diferenciar a ampla participação das mulheres com as bandeiras que as candidatas defendem.

"Isso não significa invalidar a importância de se eleger pessoas dos mais diferentes grupos sociais, da forma mais próxima possível da composição da população", complementa.

Se, por um lado, as eleições podem identificar um eleitorado mais conservador, que tende a apoiar mulheres que expressam esses ideais. Por outro, os motivos para esse voto podem se misturar com aspectos comuns a outras características da extrema-direita, como o antipetismo e críticas ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

Ela destaca ainda que os efeitos de mais mulheres eleitas varia "porque nesse grupo há pessoas com visões de mundo e interesses distintos e mesmo opostos".

A deputada distritial Bia Kicis e a ex-primeira-dama Michelle Bolsonaro — Foto: Zack Stencil/PL

É essa pluralidade que aparece na fala de Bia Kicis. Procurada pelo g1 , a deputada afirma que as críticas ao feminismo diz respeito a "ideias que não concorda" – e que defender as mulheres "não exige adesão a uma corrente ideológica".

"Defender os direitos das mulheres não exige adesão a uma corrente ideológica. As mulheres têm opiniões, valores e prioridades diferentes, e essa diversidade também precisa ser respeitada. Meu compromisso é trabalhar por todas, com atenção à segurança, à saúde e às oportunidades, para que cada mulher tenha liberdade para escolher seu caminho e condições para seguir em frente", afirmou.

O g1 tentou ouvir Michelle Bolsonaro (PL), Leila do Vôlei (PDT) e Erika Kokay (PT) sobre o resultado das eleições para o Senado, mas não recebeu retorno.

articles.title: Nomes conhecidos na política chegam ao Congresso após 1ª eleição | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento do g1 identificou 33 eleitos na primeira candidatura. Grupo reúne ex-ministros, ex-primeiras-damas, dirigentes partidários e familiares de políticos.
articles.summary: Ex-ministros, ex-primeiras-damas e familiares de políticos estão entre os eleitos na primeira candidatura. Conheça as trajetórias e veja os votos.
articles.body:
A eleição de 2026 vai levar ao Congresso alguns nomes que já eram conhecidos dos brasileiros antes de aparecerem na urna pela primeira vez. Entre eles estão a ex-primeira-dama Michelle Bolsonaro (PL), as ex-ministras Nísia Trindade (PT) e Anielle Franco (PT) e o ex-ministro Jader Filho (MDB).

Um levantamento do g1 com base nos dados de candidaturas do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) identificou 33 eleitos em sua primeira disputa eleitoral: quatro senadores e 29 deputados federais.

Embora tenham feito sua estreia na urna, são pessoas com trajetórias na política, com cargos em ministérios, governos estaduais, prefeituras e partidos, além de participação em organizações e movimentos sociais. Há também membros de famílias com presença consolidada na política.

Infográfico mostra os 33 eleitos em sua primeira disputa eleitoral em 2026: 29 deputados federais e quatro senadores — Foto: Equipe de Arte/g1

Michelle Bolsonaro (PL), Gracinha Caiado (União) e Marina JHC (PSDB) eleitas senadoras em 2026 — Foto: Montagem/g1

Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) conquistou 938.496 votos em sua primeira eleição e garantiu uma vaga no Senado pelo Distrito Federal. Mulher do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, ela foi primeira-dama entre 2019 e 2022 e, depois, assumiu o comando do PL Mulher. Sua atuação partidária e participação em campanhas de aliadas e aliados antecederam a candidatura parlamentar.

Em Goiás, Gracinha Caiado (União Brasil) se elegeu senadora ao receber 1.458.522 votos. Mulher de Ronaldo Caiado , ela já havia participado da articulação política do marido e ocupado funções na área social do governo goiano. Foi presidente de honra da Organização das Voluntárias de Goiás, coordenou o Gabinete de Políticas Sociais e participou da criação do Goiás Social.

Marina JHC (PSDB), eleita senadora em Alagoas com 926.860 votos, foi primeira-dama de Maceió durante a gestão do marido, João Henrique Caldas, o JHC, eleito governador de Alagoas neste ano. A conexão familiar também aparece na chapa: sua primeira suplente é a senadora Eudócia Caldas, mãe de JHC.

Bruno Scheid (PL) fez 474.226 votos para se eleger senador por Rondônia. Embora tenha concorrido pela primeira vez, já mantinha proximidade com Jair Bolsonaro e usou o nome Bruno Bolsonaro Scheid na campanha.

Ex-ministros estreiam na disputa eleitoral

Anielle Franco, Nísia Trindade e Jader Filho, ex-ministros da gestão Lula III, eleitos à Câmara dos Deputados — Foto: Montagem/g1

Nísia Trindade (PT-RJ) chega à Câmara dos Deputados com uma carreira construída na ciência e na gestão pública. Socióloga, foi a primeira mulher a presidir a Fundação Oswaldo Cruz e a comandar o Ministério da Saúde. Sua passagem pela Fiocruz incluiu o enfrentamento da pandemia de Covid-19. Ela deixou o ministério em 2025 e recebeu 67.350 votos na eleição deste ano.

Também eleita pelo Rio, Anielle Franco (PT) obteve 149.726 votos. Professora, jornalista e ex-ministra da Igualdade Racial, ela dirigiu o Instituto Marielle Franco e ganhou projeção na luta por justiça após o assassinato da irmã, vereadora do Rio, em 2018. Sua trajetória reúne atuação na educação, no movimento negro e no governo federal.

Jader Filho (MDB-PA), eleito com 326.617 votos, combina experiência ministerial, direção partidária e vínculos familiares. Ex-ministro das Cidades, é filho do ex-deputado, ex-senador e ex-governador Jader Barbalho e de Elcione Barbalho e irmão de Helder Barbalho, também ex-governador e eleito senador. Antes de assumir o ministério no governo Lula, presidiu o MDB paraense, coordenou campanhas do partido e administrou o grupo RBA de Comunicação.

Famílias políticas ganham novos representantes

Em Alagoas, Alvinho Lira (PP) foi eleito deputado federal com 172.628 votos, aos 20 anos. É filho de Arthur Lira , ex-presidente da Câmara, que conquistou uma vaga no Senado nesta eleição. Pai e filho ocuparão, portanto, cadeiras nas duas Casas do Congresso.

Alvinho Lira e Arthur Lira — Foto: Divulgação/PP

Na Bahia, Daniel Alencar (PSD) é filho do senador Otto Alencar e irmão de Otto Alencar Filho, que deixou a Câmara para integrar o Tribunal de Contas do Estado. Médico, Daniel foi eleito deputado federal com 192.492 votos. Outro estreante baiano, Carlos Muniz (PSDB), é filho do vereador de mesmo nome que preside a Câmara Municipal de Salvador. Ele recebeu 141.762 votos.

Os senadores Otto e Daniel Alencar (PSD) — Foto: Reprodução

Em Minas Gerais, Vinicius Diniz (PL), eleito deputado federal, é filho do deputado federal Hercílio Diniz e integra a família proprietária da rede de supermercados Coelho Diniz.

Luisa Cela (PT) e ex-governadora Izolda Cela — Foto: Reprodução

Em Pernambuco, Gabriel Porto (PSB), eleito deputado federal, é filho de Álvaro Porto, presidente da Assembleia Legislativa do estado. Em Roraima, o futuro deputado Rodrigo Mesquita (Podemos) é filho de Disney Mesquita, empresário e ex-chefe da Casa Civil do governo estadual.

Gabriel Porto (PSB) e o pai, Álvaro Porto, presidente da Assembleia Legislativa, reeleito para o terceiro mandato — Foto: Reprodução

Márcio Rezende (PSD) é irmão do prefeito de Macaé, Welberth Rezende. — Foto: Reprodução

Advogado e dirigente partidário, recebeu 155.836 votos. Seu caso mostra como alguém pode estrear nas urnas depois de exercer influência sobre candidaturas e alianças.

Thiago Ganem (PL-MG), cujo nome completo é Thiago Martins Milhim, também tinha experiência em governos e partidos. Foi secretário de Esportes na Prefeitura de São Paulo e ocupou uma secretaria no Ministério do Esporte no governo Lula em 2023. O nome de urna o associa ao grupo político Ganem, sem que isso represente parentesco com a família.

Secretário-geral do Podemos e ex-secretário nacional do Ministério dos Esportes, Thiago Ganem recebeu a medalha da Inconfidência Mineira em novembro de 2025 — Foto: Reprodução

Outros eleitos passaram por cargos de gestão antes de disputar votos:

Dra. Erica (Podemos-AP): médica pediatra e neonatologista, ocupou a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Macapá.

Vinicius Ferro (MDB-MA): comandou a Secretaria de Planejamento e Orçamento do Maranhão.

Rodrigo Tavares (PL-MG): dirigiu o Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem de Minas Gerais.

Coronel Roveri (Podemos-MT): foi secretário de Segurança Pública de Mato Grosso.

Delegado Felipe Curi (PP-RJ): comandou a Secretaria de Polícia Civil do Rio de Janeiro.

Delegado Charles (PV-PI): ganhou projeção à frente do Departamento de Repressão às Ações Criminosas Organizadas, o Draco, da Polícia Civil do Piauí.

Elias Jabbour (PCdoB-RJ): professor da Uerj, foi consultor do banco dos Brics e presidiu o Instituto Pereira Passos, da Prefeitura do Rio.

Redes sociais, militância e atividade empresarial

Ana Elisa de Divinópolis, é a deputada mais jovem da Câmara de Deputados — Foto: Ana Elisa/Reprodução Redes Sociais

Ana Elisa (PT-MG), eleita aos 21 anos, recebeu 524.219 votos. Estudante de Direito de Divinópolis, ganhou espaço nas redes sociais com debates sobre direitos, educação, feminismo e combate ao racismo.

No Paraná, Jeffrey Chiquini (Novo) conquistou 425.399 votos. Advogado, ficou conhecido pela defesa de Filipe Martins, ex-assessor de Jair Bolsonaro, e levou para a campanha críticas ao Supremo Tribunal Federal.

Julia de Castro (PL-RJ), historiadora e vice-presidente nacional do PL Jovem. — Foto: Reprodução

Julia de Castro (PL-RJ), historiadora, já atuava como vice-presidente nacional do PL Jovem. Sua primeira candidatura ocorreu, portanto, depois da participação na organização partidária.

A lista inclui ainda empresários que levaram suas trajetórias profissionais à campanha. Felipe Show (União Brasil-AP) construiu sua atuação no comércio amapaense. Ditinho Avivip (União Brasil-BA), nome de urna de Benedito de Souza Lemos Filho, tem trajetória empresarial em Santo Antônio de Jesus e região.

Estreantes no Congresso, conhecidos na política. 33 eleitos em 2026 são ex-ministros, ex-primeiras-damas e familiares de políticos. — Foto: Montagem/g1

articles.title: Caso Master completa um mês suspenso na presidência do STF com pedidos de soltura e apuração aguardando análise | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigadores e defesas criticam indefinição sobre medidas que dependem do aval da Suprema Corte. Mendonça segue como relator, mas casos estão vinculados a Fachin.
articles.summary: Investigadores e defesas criticam indefinição sobre medidas que dependem do aval da Suprema Corte. Mendonça segue como relator, mas casos estão vinculados a Fachin.
articles.body:
Investigadores e advogados apontam que a suspensão do caso Master pela presidência do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) está represando pedidos da Polícia Federal para avançar nas investigações, além da análise sobre a manutenção ou não da prisão de investigados.

No dia 12 de setembro, o presidente do Supremo, Luiz Edson Fachin , determinou que o ministro André Mendonça enviasse à Presidência todos os processos relacionados às investigações do Master , que apura supostas fraudes financeiras, além de corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro, coação, vazamento de dados sigilosos e o envolvimento de autoridades com o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro.

A medida foi tomada em meio à crise institucional instalada no Supremo após Mendonça determinar à PF a elaboração de um relatório sobre as conexões de Daniel Vorcaro com Alexandre de Moraes .

Também foram levantadas, por aliados de Moraes, acusações de que o relator do Master estaria direcionando as investigações , o que Mendonça nega.

Do dia 12 de setembro para cá, investigadores ouvidos pelo g1 afirmam que a Polícia Federal manteve o ritmo das linhas de apuração dentro de suas atribuições, tocando medidas que estavam pendentes e análises de materiais.

Mas policiais reconhecem que há representações, como novos pedidos que dependem do aval da Justiça, paradas no Supremo. O teor desse material, no entanto, é mantido em reserva para não prejudicar o andamento das investigações.

Interlocutores de Mendonça também afirmam que, desde o envio dos processos para a Presidência, não foram tomadas novas medidas .

A indefinição sobre novos desdobramentos ocorre porque Fachin, na prática, paralisou os casos, mas manteve Mendonça na relatoria. Havia uma expectativa de que Fachin liberasse pedidos urgentes para o gabinete do relator, mas isso não tem ocorrido.

No dia 25 de setembro, o presidente do Supremo solicitou que a Procuradoria-Geral da República se manifestasse sobre questões pendentes, como revogações de prisões e sigilos de comunicações. Outro ponto em questão é definir se cabe a Fachin ou a Mendonça decidir sobre essas demandas.

No STF, há expectativa de que após as eleições as investigações retomem o fluxo normal .

A defesa de Daniel Vorcaro disse que chegou a pedir uma audiência com Fachin, mas foi informada por e-mail que medidas urgentes deveriam ser enviadas para Mendonça.

Na última quarta-feira (7), estiveram no gabinete do relator do Master reforçando o pedido de liberdade e foram informados de que os processos estavam na Presidência.

O gabinete de Mendonça, ainda segundo a defesa, teria repassado que "há mais de duas semanas, teria sido encaminhado um ofício, ao que parece ainda sem resposta, requerendo a devolução dos autos para apreciação de pedidos urgentes pendentes de análise". Os advogados defenderam a liberação do pedido para análise de Mendonça.

Henrique Vorcaro : pediu para suspender o envio do caso Master à Presidência do STF, a fim de permitir a análise de seu pedido de soltura;

Fabiano Zettel : pediu a revisão da prisão preventiva;

Felipe Vorcaro : pediu para retirar a suspensão do caso na Presidência, permitindo que o ministro André Mendonça analise seu pedido de revogação da prisão;

Daniel Lopes Monteiro : pediu a revogação da prisão;

André Mendonça : apresentou manifestação sobre o relatório utilizado pelo ministro Alexandre de Moraes em relação a ele;

OAB : pediu garantia do sigilo das comunicações relacionadas à atuação de advogados que eventualmente estejam abrangidas pelo material arrecadado no âmbito da investigação.

Ministro Edson Fachin — Foto: Alejandro Zambrana/STF

articles.title: Bracing for the midterms, Trump says he will be blamed if Republicans lose
articles.summary: CLARKSVILLE, Tenn. — Even as he makes a case that Republicans should win the midterm congressional elections, President Donald Trump is bracing for the fallout should they lose.
articles.body: CLARKSVILLE, Tenn. — Even as he makes a case that Republicans should win the midterm congressional elections, President Donald Trump is bracing for the fallout should they lose. Someone is bound to get blamed, and Trump said at a rally in Tennessee on Saturday that he expects it will be him. “If we don’t win the midterms, they’re going to blame me,” Trump said. “You know that. And if we do win them, I will get no credit whatsoever. It’s true. I won’t get any.” “But I’m working my ass off,” he added. “You better get out there and vote.” Trump is in “grind it out mode” ahead of the midterms, a person familiar with the matter said, and is prepared for the worst-case election outcome. Midterm elections often punish the sitting president’s party, and Trump’s popularity isn’t helping the GOP’s cause. Only 38% approve of his performance in office, compared with 59% who disapprove, according to an NBC News average of polls. Trump is looking to defy historical trends by motivating core supporters who might be inclined to sit out the elections, and by offering voters an unusual sweetener if they preserve the Republican majority in the House and Senate. He closed his hour-and-a-half-long speech with a reminder that “with your vote on November 3rd, you’ll get $5,000.” That’s the size of the check he’s promising to send adults if Republicans win the midterms. The total price tag is estimated at $1.3 trillion. Trump is indeed pushing himself as the elections approach, keeping up a frenetic schedule. Tennessee was the seventh different state he has visited since the start of October. He had planned to fly to an eighth, Alabama, later in the day to attend the Georgia-Alabama football game, but canceled the trip with Hurricane Isaias bearing down. Trump used part of the rally to debunk the idea that his popularity has dropped. In a social media post Saturday, he wrote that the notion that he’s in disfavor is a “false narrative.” On stage, he played a CNN clip showing that his support among his MAGA supporters is nearly unanimous and has shown no slippage since the 2024 elections. (CNN was one of three news outlets that the Trump administration last month banned from White House grounds). “I’m very popular, I really am,” Trump told the crowd. For Trump, traveling to a deep-red congressional district in a deep-red state like Tennessee might seem like time wasted in the few weeks left before the midterms. Republicans are expected to sweep the state’s House and Senate races. Trump’s rally took place in an indoor arena in a northern Tennessee county that he won by 18 percentage points in the 2024 presidential race. Trump himself suggested the state’s congressional candidates are already on a glide path to victory, with or without him. “These guys are all going to win,” he said. “These congressmen are phenomenal. So, I’m saying, ‘What the hell am I doing in Tennessee?’” Answering his own question, he said he wanted to “reward the places that have automatically treated you well.” Trump won Tennessee in all three of his presidential campaigns. Other Republicans said Trump is hewing to a sensible strategy: mobilizing up his supporters and making sure they vote on Nov. 3 even though he’s not on the ballot. “It rallies the base,” Rep. Tim Burchett, R-Tenn., said in an interview before Trump took the stage. “And that’s really what we’ve got to see in a midterm election. That’s what you’ve got to have: the base.” Much of Trump’s address was a recitation of what he considers his chief accomplishments. He cited a rise in the median household income in his first year in office and a drop in the nation’s poverty rate. Never shy about rebranding American landmarks, he also mused about renaming the Atlantic or Pacific oceans in ways that would ensure he’s not forgotten. Presumably in jest, he said, “We call it, ‘Trump Ocean.’ Or, ‘Ocean of the Americas,’ something like that. No, we have to. We should have before I get out, I think we should have an ocean and we need a great river.”

"It rallies the base," Rep. Tim Burchett, R-Tenn., said in an interview before Trump took the stage. "And that's really what we've got to see in a midterm election. That's what you've got to have: the base."

Much of Trump's address was a recitation of what he considers his chief accomplishments. He cited a rise in the median household income in his first year in office and a drop in the nation's poverty rate.

Never shy about rebranding American landmarks, he also mused about renaming the Atlantic or Pacific oceans in ways that would ensure he's not forgotten.

Presumably in jest, he said, "We call it, 'Trump Ocean.' Or, 'Ocean of the Americas,' something like that. No, we have to. We should have before I get out, I think we should have an ocean and we need a great river."

articles.title: Justice Department investigating television networks over Trump pool coverage
articles.summary: The White House had blocked access for CNN, MS Now and Politico, leading them to restrict pool coverage.
articles.body:
The US justice department (DoJ) has said it is investigating several television networks over whether they broke federal competition laws when they recently suspended pool coverage of President Donald Trump.

Last month, five networks temporarily suspended presidential coverage for several days in response to the Trump administration withdrawing the credentials of reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico.

The Justice Department asked ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News to hand over communications related to the pool and said that the boycott could violate the Sherman Act, referring to a law that bars companies from engaging in monopolistic business practices.

Pool members ordinarily share their material with the wider media.

A DoJ spokesperson said: "The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these ​news organisations have violated the antitrust laws."

The television networks have not yet commented.

Trump blocked CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House last month after accusing the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his team.

The White House later reinstated their access after a ruling from a judge. The three outlets had sued the Trump administration, arguing the restricted access violated their First Amendment rights.

The First Amendment forbids the government from "abridging" the freedom of the press - language that courts have traditionally interpreted as preventing the government from discriminating against the media based on the content of their coverage.

The Trump administration has taken a number of legal actions against news publications in the US, including lawsuits over coverage of the president.

In February, the White House announced it was taking control of the press pool which has access to Trump and had for more than a century been managed by the White House Correspondents' Association.

The same month, the Trump administration moved to bar Associated Press (AP) reporters and photographers from spaces where access is limited, such as the Oval Office or Air Force One, because of the outlet's usage of the term "Gulf of Mexico" instead of "Gulf of America". AP filed a lawsuit and the case remains ongoing.

articles.title: Trump announces Katie Bailey to lead White House outreach to Congress
articles.summary: President Donald Trump on Saturday named Katie Bailey to lead the White House’s Office of Legislative Affairs, appointing her to be the liaison between the administration and Congress.
articles.body: President Donald Trump on Saturday named Katie Bailey to lead the White House’s Office of Legislative Affairs, appointing her to be the liaison between the administration and Congress. “After previously working on Capitol Hill, Katie understands how the Executive and Legislative Branches of Government can most effectively work together to achieve Great Success for the American People,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. Trump added that Bailey is currently his deputy director of legislative affairs, liaising with the Senate and, per Trump, helping with the confirmations of Cabinet members including Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. Bailey’s LinkedIn profile says she previously served as special assistant to the president from September 2025 to June 2026. She also served in numerous legislative roles on Capitol Hill, most recently as legislative director for Sen. Mike Braun, R-Ind. Bailey’s appointment comes a day after Trump named Katie Zacharia to be his new White House press secretary. James Braid previously led the office, helping navigate Trump’s legislative priorities through Congress, a job that could become harder if Republicans fail to conserve their majority in both chambers after the midterms. Braid, Trump said Sunday, was his “longest tenured” legislative affairs director. The president said Braid had done a “fabulous job, and is now going into the private sector.” Trump announced Braid’s exit in late August, saying Braid would leave in September. In a post on X at the time, Braid said he was “profoundly grateful” to Trump and Vice President JD Vance. Braid had served as Vance’s top policy aide and deputy chief of staff while he was a senator. Vance had called Braid’s role “one of the toughest jobs in the entire Administration.”

articles.title: Justice Department investigating major TV networks over suspending pool coverage of Trump
articles.summary: The Justice Department said it is investigating five major TV broadcast networks for potentially violating federal antitrust laws after the networks temporarily declined to provide pool coverage of President Donald Trump, a department spokesperson said.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — The Justice Department said it is investigating five major TV broadcast networks for potentially violating federal antitrust laws after the networks temporarily declined to provide pool coverage of President Donald Trump, a department spokesperson said. The investigation into the networks that make up the White House TV press pool — NBC, ABC, CBS, CNN and Fox News — is underway, and the department sent out “civil investigative demands” on Friday, according to a Justice Department official. “Members of the television press pool have boycotted covering White House events. Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act. The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws,” department spokeswoman Emily Covington said Saturday. The pool is a rotating group of networks that share duties of recording the president’s activities during public appearances and travel. The network performing pool duty then distributes information and media, such as video footage and audio, to other outlets. The New York Times first reported the investigation. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ABC News said it has not received any notification from the Justice Department but expects to. Representatives for NBC, CBS and CNN declined to comment. Fox did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The investigation appears to be the latest move from the White House in its escalating feud against the press corps. Last month, Trump barred CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House grounds, citing what he said was “their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” The other networks in the TV pool briefly declined to participate in pool duties after CNN was removed from its spot in the rotation. CNN, MS Now and Politico sued against the ban, claiming it was a violation of the First Amendment. They were reinstated about a week later after a judge ruled that the administration had to temporarily restore their access for 14 days. A federal judge this week extended the order to Tuesday. The five major networks released a joint statement at the time, saying, “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.” The pool system has been recognized by administrations from both parties for decades, and the coverage is used by pool members and subscribers, which includes outlets like Newsmax, One America News Network, C-SPAN and international outlets. During the time the outlets declined to provide pool coverage, individual TV networks, including NBC News, continued to provide coverage of White House events that were open to the press, outside of the pool. Bruce D. Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said in a statement that the First Amendment protects the decisions news organizations make about coverage, and called the investigation “another and even more brazen attempt to try to intimidate journalists.” Kelly O’Donnell reported from Washington, and Marlene Lenthang from Los Angeles.

articles.title: Trump continues red state campaign swing with Montana, Arizona rallies next week
articles.summary: President Trump will continue his red state campaign swing with recently announced rallies in Montana and Arizona slated for this week with important races in each state just under a month away. The Arizona rally is tentatively planned to be hosted at Laughlin Bullhead International Airport in Bullhead City – a town near the Nevada border…
articles.body:
President Trump will continue his red state campaign swing with recently announced rallies in Montana and Arizona slated for this week with important races in each state just under a month away.

The Arizona rally is tentatively planned to be hosted at Laughlin Bullhead International Airport in Bullhead City – a town near the Nevada border – where Trump will take the stage on Oct. 14 at 1 p.m., according to the Arizona Republic , citing a now-deleted post on the Republican National Committee’s website.

It is unclear who will appear alongside Trump at the Bullhead City rally, but the Arizona GOP is looking to regain the Grand Canyon State’s governorship after previously having a tight grip on Arziona’s statewide offices, but faces tough political headwinds.

Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs (D) is up for reelection after winning in 2022, but Arizona is one of five Democratic-held governorships up this year in states won by Trump in 2024.

Hobbs will face off against Republican Rep. Andy Biggs (Ariz.), a House Freedom Caucus member backed by President Trump.

Trump’s Montana rally is reportedly set for the Majestic Valley Arena in Flathead County as he campaigns for Republican candidate Aaron Flint in the Big Sky Country’s 1st Congressional District election. Trump will speak in Montana on Oct. 12 at 6:15 p.m., according to KPAX , citing a source familiar with the matter.

Flint is running against Democratic candidate Sam Forstag to replace retiring Rep. Ryan Zinke (R-Mont.).

Montana’s Senate race has also remained somewhat competitive as Democratic candidate Alani Bankhead, GOP nominee Kurt Alme, independent Seth Bodnar and Libertarian Kyle Austin compete for retiring Sen. Steve Daines (R-Mont.) open Senate seat.

Despite early polling showing Bodnar could beat Alme in a one-on-one race, Bankhead has repeated that she would not drop out of the race to assist Bodnar’s chance, saying in August, “I’ll never bow down…I am in this race to win it, and I am staying through Nov. 3.”

According to Rutgers-Eagleton polling from September, 38 percent of respondents backed Alme, 30 percent supported Bodnar, 16 percent chose Bankhead and 5 percent supported Austin.

Trump’s tour of traditionally red states like Montana and Nebraska has raised some eyebrows but one Republican source told The Hill earlier this month that the trips were part of a larger strategy of replicating the party’s presidential election turnout as much as they can going into the midterms, comparing it to “hitting two birds with one stone.”

VETERAN SHOT 7 TIMES IN FORT HOOD MASSACRE HAS A WARNING FOR AMERICANS PLANNING TO WATCH EXECUTION "There are two thoughts: don't show it and show it," he continued. articles.title: Trump says he'd 'love' to have Sen. John Fetterman as a Republican amid growing speculation
articles.summary: President Donald Trump called Sen. John Fetterman a "great guy" and said he would welcome the Pennsylvania Democrat into the Republican Party ranks.
articles.body: President Donald Trump praised Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., as a "great guy" on Saturday, saying he would welcome the Pennsylvania Democrat into the Republican Party. Trump was asked by a reporter after stepping off Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews whether he had spoken to Fetterman — who has repeatedly broken with Democrats during the current session of Congress — about becoming a Republican and whether he would welcome such a switch. "I'd love to see it. I think he's great," Trump responded. "It's going to be hard for him to get the nomination as a Democrat, but I'd love to have him as a Republican," he continued. REPUBLICANS SAY THEY'D WELCOME FETTERMAN AS GOP EYES BIGGER SENATE MAJORITY Trump described Fetterman as a "great guy" with "magnificent parents," whom he said he had spoken with previously. "He's a very solid person," Trump added. "He's smart and all that, but he's got great common sense." Trump also suggested that switching parties could benefit Fetterman politically. "If you look at the polls, he does better as a Republican than he does as a Democrat," he said. MAVERICK DEMOCRAT SURGES WITH REPUBLICANS AS HIS OWN PARTY TURNS ON HIM, STOKING TALK OF GOP SWITCH Trump's comments come as Fetterman has repeatedly broken with Democrats on key issues, including the Iran war and immigration, although he continues to vote with his party the vast majority of the time. During the current session of Congress, however, that figure has fallen to just under 81%, Fox News Digital previously reported. Fetterman's occasional breaks with his party have fueled speculation in recent months about whether he might eventually become a Republican. He has also reportedly used Republican fundraising platforms to solicit donations and maintains a close friendship with Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala. Last month, Fetterman recorded a video introducing Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., at the Republican Midterm Convention. FETTERMAN TEASES WHERE HIS TRUE LOYALTY LIES AFTER SURPRISE APPEARANCE AT GOP CONVENTION He also mistakenly referred to himself as a lifelong Republican during an appearance at the Texas Tribune's TribFest last month. articles.title: US opens antitrust probe into TV networks for halting Trump coverage
articles.summary: Department of Justice says it’s investigating whether the White House press pool’s decision violated antitrust laws.
articles.body:
The United States Department of Justice has opened an investigation into television networks’ decision to halt coverage of President Donald Trump last month.

A spokesperson said on Saturday that the department was investigating whether the networks violated federal antitrust laws by their boycott, which followed a White House decision to pull the credentials of reporters from three news organisations, including CNN.

The ⁠networks under investigation are ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News, said Emily Convington, the Justice Department spokesperson.

“Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act,” she said of the antitrust legislation.

“The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws.”

The investigation is the latest in a series ‌of clashes between the Trump administration and major news organisations. Trump has repeatedly called the mainstream media “fake news” and frequently clashes with reporters during encounters with the press.

The action also puts legal and potentially financial pressure on the media to continue coverage of the president even when they disagree with how the White House handles them.

The networks did not immediately comment on the announcement.

The Justice Department’s move came after the television pool of five broadcasters last month ceased presidential coverage after the administration barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.

The White House said on September 19 that covering the president was a “privilege – not a right”. The outlets ⁠sued the administration, alleging the exclusions violated the First Amendment and that the White House was retaliating over their coverage.

CNN is one of the five ⁠news organisations – along with ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC – ⁠that make up the primary White House television pool .

They share the costs of covering the president, take turns organising coverage, and share the footage with outlets around the country.

All of the five television networks that cover the White House, including Fox ‌News, suspended coverage in solidarity and refused to provide replacement coverage.

The White House reinstated the credentials on September 24 after US District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled that the ban was likely unconstitutional and ‌ordered ‌the administration to “immediately return, reinstate, and restore” their access.

However, disputes over access to specific presidential events and pool assignments continued.

Jose Zamora, the Committee to Protect Journalists’ Americas director, on Saturday criticised the administration’s decision to investigate.

“The government should not use antitrust investigations to intimidate news outlets defending press access,” Zamora said on X. “The public’s right to know depends on that access.”

articles.title: Drumcree: It's within DUP's gift to remove O'Neill as first minister, says Lockhart
articles.summary: Carla Lockhart says unionist voters are angry at Michelle O'Neill over her role in the Garvaghy Road protests.
articles.body:
A DUP MP says unionist voters are angry at Michelle O'Neill over her role in the Garvaghy Road protests and says it "cannot be business as usual" at Stormont.

Carla Lockhart said the DUP has it "within its gift to remove" O'Neill as Northern Ireland's first minister.

On Friday, the secretary of state banned the Portadown District Lodge from marching down the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road . His decision was welcomed by nationalist politicians but unionists have criticised the move.

O'Neill is one of a number of Sinn Féin politicians who have confirmed they received letters from the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) investigating protests over the Drumcree parading dispute.

What is the Garvaghy Road dispute all about?

Four key takeaways from the Drumcree dispute so far

Speaking outside Drumcree Church on Saturday, Lockhart said her constituents are angry.

"They're angry at the chief constable for allowing lawlessness to win, for allowing the mob to dictate," she said.

"They're angry at the secretary of state for his intervention, but the most palpable anger is at Michelle O'Neill, this self-proclaimed 'first minister for all' for breaking the law flagrantly on the Garvaghy Road, and thumbing her nose at unionism and at the Orange Order and at this community."

Police had repeatedly warned those taking part in the unnotified protest that they could be liable for arrest.

O'Neill has defended her involvement, saying she was standing with the local community in opposition to an Orange Order parade through the area.

She previously dismissed a call from the DUP to resign over her role in protests telling the assembly she was "proud" to stand with the residents and "will continue to stand with them".

'It cannot be business as usual at Stormont'

The DUP (Democratic Unionist Party) share power with Sinn Féin in the Northern Ireland Executive, but Lockhart says it can no longer be business as usual.

"You can not continue to engage with someone who is so blatant in her disregard and disdain for a large section of this community," she said.

"Very clearly it cannot be business as usual at Stormont."

Lockhart says her party must take action against O'Neill.

"People want to see consequences, and we have said very clearly, profound consequence, and therefore we should use whatever is in our armoury to ensure that Michelle O'Neill, the person who really is supposed to be that first minister for all, as she claims, is dealt with in the appropriate way," she added.

The DUP could remove O'Neill from the first minister's position if the deputy first minister quits.

That role is held by Emma Little-Pengelly, but that seems unlikely.

DUP leader Gavin Robinson said that Lockhart "is right that the options are there", but stopped short of suggesting his party may collapse the executive.

Speaking on BBC News NI's Sunday Politics programme , he echoed Lockhart's words that "it will not be business as usual", but added: "does collapsing Stormont bring the Orangemen home"?

Robinson also called on the chief constable to "be very open" in telling the public "what was the threat that he perceived" when he asked the secretary of state to review the Parades Commission's determination.

He said he "certainly wouldn't" want Sir Chris to govern Northern Ireland if the executive did collapse.

TUV leader Jim Allister said he was "disappointed" by the DUP's "limp response".

He said Robinson promised "profound consequences, and then when he's asked what they are, it emerges that the Emperor of the DUP has no clothes".

Allister accused the DUP of "doing nothing", which he said showed "there are no political consequences" for Sinn Féin.

Sinn Féin assembly member John O'Dowd rejected claims that the move to ban the parade went in favour of his party, saying "the decision went in the way of the residents" who he said have "faced an awful four weeks" since the application to walk was lodged.

O'Dowd, who is also finance minister in the executive, was one of a number of Sinn Féin politicians who joined a protest with residents on the Garvaghy Road.

On Thursday, the police said they had begun issuing letters inviting people "reasonably suspected" of committing offences linked to the protests to interview.

Speaking on BBC News NI's Sunday Politics programme , O'Dowd said: "I own my decision", adding that he thinks it was "the right thing to do".

"I got into politics to stand against the intimidation of communities such as the Garvaghy Road, who went through hell and high water over many, many years.

"I stood with the people of the Garvaghy Road. I will continue to stand with the people of Garvaghy Road because it was the right thing to do."

He added that he believes the community responded in "a peaceful, democratic way" to the decision to approve a march on 27 September.

"I would appeal, not only to Gavin, but maybe hopelessly to Carla and others, to calm their language and to show responsible leadership and calm leadership at this stage," he added.

"I don't think that continued demonisation or an attempt to criminalise the community of the Garvaghy Road is an appropriate way forward.

"What we need in Portadown is reconciliation."

That parade did not happen and, after a series of legal challenges and talks between residents and Orangemen, the secretary of state banned the procession on Friday.

The secretary of state said he received advice from the PSNI chief constable that allowing the procession to go ahead could lead to serious injury, disorder and wider unrest .

On Saturday, a High Court judge said a legal appeal by Orangemen following the secretary of state's decision was not an emergency case and adjourned the hearing until Monday.

Lockhart said the 35 Orangemen from Portadown District Lodge had "stood lawfully" for the last two weeks on Drumcree hill.

"I've been on this hill from I was 10 years of age, it means something to me. It means a lot to my constituents here in Upper Bann," she said.

So does the Upper Bann MP still have confidence in her own party?

"I have confidence that I will ensure that my constituents' voices are heard within the party, and I will ensure that I continue to represent the views here in Portadown," she said.

articles.title: California faces unlikely tax revolt amid billions in illegal immigrant healthcare costs
articles.summary: California Medicaid costs drive Gavin Newsom's new health insurance tax, but doctors and insurers sue claiming it violates Proposition 35.
articles.body: As California grapples with soaring Medi-Cal costs — including billions spent on healthcare for immigrants without legal status — Gov. Gavin Newsom and Democratic lawmakers have backed a revised health-plan tax in response to new federal restrictions, a move critics warn could shift more costs onto privately insured Californians. The tax has united an unlikely coalition of doctors and health insurers against him, with critics warning it could make California even more expensive. To preserve billions in Medi-Cal financing after Washington tightened the rules governing health-plan taxes used to draw federal matching funds, Newsom backed a redesigned tax that would raise the levy on private health plans beginning in 2027 if federally approved, potentially increasing premiums for their customers. Providing healthcare to illegal immigrants cost California an estimated $12.4 billion in 2025, the Associated Press reported. When asked if expanding coverage to illegal immigrants created a need for California to raise taxes, Brian Blase, president of the right-of-center Paragon Health Institute, answered with a strong "yes." DR. OZ UNVEILS MEDICAID OVERHAUL, CLAMPS DOWN ON $2B FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS AND MANDATES WORK FOR ABLE-BODIED "The One Big Beautiful Bill Act limited California's ability to target the tax just on Medicaid insurers, so California is proposing to raise the health insurance tax on people that have private coverage ... the estimates are that would increase insurance for families by $400 a year," he told Fox News Digital. "That is just because California doesn't want to deal with its unsustainable spending ... there are many people on the program who are not eligible for the program, and that is not even accounting for the fact that California has expanded Medicaid to all unauthorized immigrants in the state." California's attempt to shore up Medi-Cal's bottom line follows federal changes that will prevent the state from continuing its existing health-plan tax structure after 2026, forcing a redesign of a financing mechanism that has generated billions of dollars for the program. The California Medical Association and California Association of Health Plans are suing to block the tax increase, not on the grounds that it benefits illegal immigrants, but over allegations that the measure violates voter-approved limits on health-plan taxes and restrictions on how the resulting revenue can be spent. The duo uniting to challenge the tax is notable because doctors and insurance companies often find themselves on opposite sides of healthcare debates. Proposition 35, the initiative in question, limits how much California can tax commercial health-plan enrollment, constraining the state's options as it tries to comply with new federal rules governing the much higher tax previously imposed on Medi-Cal enrollment. The proposition was passed with overwhelming support from Californian voters. NEWSOM BEGS CALIFORNIANS TO VOTE 'NO' ON BILLIONAIRE'S TAX IN FACE OF MASS EXODUS, PITCHES NATIONWIDE TAX HIKE "California voters passed Proposition 35 and made it law. The state does not get to ignore that law simply because following the law is inconvenient," California Medical Association CEO Dustin Corcoran said in a statement. Health insurers warn the cost of the revised tax could be passed directly on to consumers through higher premiums, estimating an increase of about $100 per person per year. A family of four, for example, could face an additional $400 annually on top of normal rate increases. Newsom spokeswoman Tara Gallegos said that the governor maintains that his tax increase is not rendered illegal by the proposition. "The state disagrees with their claims, and we believe the courts will too," she told Fox News Digital of the lawsuit. H.D. Palmer, deputy director for external affairs at the California Department of Finance, explained to Fox News Digital that the new tax measure was designed to comply with the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. According to Palmer, the state's current health tax regime may conflict with the bill and that the state is submitting a proposal with two tracks — one that is similar to the current taxing scheme but might run afoul of federal law and another that conforms to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act by shifting costs toward private plans. CALIFORNIANS FLEEING TO RED STATES ARE DRIVING UP HOME PRICES AND RENTS IN THEIR NEW CITIES, DATA SHOWS "If the federal government declines to approve the tax that is structured similar to the existing [health plan tax], Proposition 35 may then sunset per current law," he added. California has faced a mass exodus of people and businesses over the past decade, with the cost of living being one of the chief reasons individuals cite for leaving the Golden State. One analysis found that almost 10 million people moved from California to other states between 2010 and 2024, while just over 7 million moved to California from elsewhere in the country during the same period. articles.title: How a lobsterman's privacy fight reached SCOTUS — and could ripple far beyond the water: 'Ain't over yet'
articles.summary: Frank Thompson calls GPS tracking on his lobster boat a 24/7 "ankle bracelet" after the Supreme Court declined to hear his Fourth Amendment case.
articles.body: One Maine lobsterman isn’t ready to give up after the Supreme Court declined to hear his challenge to a GPS vessel-tracking requirement Monday, fearing it threatens a way of life passed down for generations and could ripple across other industries. For decades, fifth-generation lobsterman Frank Thompson has driven his boat from Vinalhaven, a small island off the Maine coast, into deeper waters to set traps and haul in lobsters. Now, he says a GPS tracking mandate has turned his boat into a government-issued 24/7 "ankle bracelet," sparking a years-long legal battle over constant surveillance and Fourth Amendment rights. "This is totally against the Fourth Amendment, and somebody's got to hear it one way or another," Thompson told Fox News Digital. "This black box that they're putting aboard the boat is not legal, in my mind, and I'm not a criminal." Thompson, who also owns Fox Island Lobster Company with his wife and two sons, was out fishing earlier this month when one of his sons texted him, letting him know the Supreme Court had declined his petition to hear the case and left in place a First Circuit ruling that said the GPS tracking requirement did not violate the Fourth Amendment because lobstering is a closely regulated industry. THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC? "I just told myself, I said, ‘Well, it ain't over yet,’" he said. The mandate, requiring a small electronic box to be installed aboard federally licensed lobster boats in Maine, has flipped Thompson’s life upside down, he said. According to the Maine Department of Marine Resources (Maine DMR), the devices collect a boat’s location once per minute while moving and every six hours while docked. The tracking doesn’t stop there, Thompson said, with the device collecting data even during personal trips, a key concern in his case. Whether Thompson is traveling back to the mainland or having a family picnic, he said the device gives him "a creepy feeling" about who has his information and who is possibly watching. "Freedom is gone. What else can they do to us?" he said. Thompson said there is even more at stake. He described how his first boat ride happened two days after he was born and how his sons and grandchildren are following in his footsteps today. FLOCK SURVEILLANCE SPREADS ACROSS THE SOUTH AS RED-STATE LAWMAKERS SEEK TO AX '1984'-STYLE TRACKING TOOLS "Fishing's been in my blood and I always want to be on the water and it's something that I couldn't explain to you the feeling that you get out fishing and stuff," he said. "It's just a way of life." Thompson equated the feeling of pulling up the line of a trap and catching dozens of lobsters to "opening a present at Christmas time." "This is what I like," he said. Matthew Gilliam, Thompson’s attorney at Pacific Legal Foundation, said lobstermen must carry the trackers "as a condition of earning a living and keeping their lobster license," arguing the mandate infringes on Fourth Amendment rights "because it was warrantless." "That forced trespass was a violation of the Fourth Amendment because it's an unreasonable search and seizure," he said. Maine DMR implemented the rule in 2023 at the direction of the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission. State officials and conservationists have since backed the mandate as necessary to protect endangered North Atlantic right whales, monitor lobster populations and sustain the industry for years to come. "They're bringing it up because it's for the whales," Thompson said. "Well, the government's lying through their teeth like they always do, and I'm not a criminal." FORMER PENTAGON AI CHIEF WARNS FLOCK CAMERAS COULD CREATE 'CHINA-LIKE SURVEILLANCE STATE' IN THE US Shortly after the mandate took effect, a federal lawsuit was filed by Thompson and four fellow lobstermen, claiming the device subjected them to tracking they never consented to. A federal judge dismissed the case, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit upheld that decision, finding the tracking requirement did not violate the Fourth Amendment under an exception for closely regulated industries. Thompson said the privacy concerns extend beyond fisheries, with the American Farm Bureau Federation (AFBF), which represents farmers and ranchers, standing behind his Supreme Court appeal. The group filed an amicus brief arguing the lower court’s reasoning could weaken Fourth Amendment protections for farmers, ranchers and others in regulated industries. "Everybody's got cell phones, they can track us if they want to," Thompson said. "But put a black box on a tractor, seeing how many days that he's out in the field or whatever, it's just, the independence is gone." Although the AFBF supported Thompson’s challenge, the Conservation Law Foundation, which filed a separate brief in favor of the tracking requirement during the First Circuit appeal, praised Monday’s decision. "This decision is a valuable step toward appropriately managing this iconic species," CLF Associate Attorney Sarah Shahabi said in a press release. Fox News Digital reached out to CLF for comment but did not hear back before publication. TEXAS GOV. GREG ABBOTT MOVES TO CUT STATE FUNDING FOR AI-POWERED FLOCK CAMERAS AMID PRIVACY CONCERNS Maine DMR also responded to the decision, maintaining its support for the tracking requirement in a statement on Monday. "DMR continues to believe this data collection requirement is critically important to the long-term sustainability of the lobster fishery and resource," Maine DMR Commissioner Carl Wilson wrote. Gilliam said that despite the Supreme Court declining to hear the case, lobstermen and others in regulated industries should not lose their privacy rights simply for doing their jobs. "Lobstermen and others have Fourth Amendment protections and we'll continue fighting against government overreach," he said. Thompson said he still wants answers about why the government is treating lobstermen like they have done something wrong. "We're just out there making a living and we're taking good care of the resource," Thompson said. "You can't believe the steps that we've done to take care of it and we don't get credit for nothing." He warned that if government regulations continue to be adopted across different fisheries, it could "ruin us." "People just don't think before they react to it," he said. "All these rules and regulations and it's taking away a lifestyle of generations of freedom." "I'm fighting for everybody, not just myself," Thompson said. "I'm just fighting for freedom for everybody."

articles.title: The Memo: As Trump lavishes cash on voters, ethics experts raise alarm
articles.summary: President Trump is doing everything he can to win favor with a dissatisfied electorate before the midterms — including promising money. Speaking in San Antonio on Wednesday evening, Trump repeated his pledge to send $5,000 to every adult American if the GOP retains its narrow majorities in the House and the Senate. Skeptics roll their…
articles.body:
President Trump is doing everything he can to win favor with a dissatisfied electorate before the midterms — including promising money.

Speaking in San Antonio on Wednesday evening, Trump repeated his pledge to send $5,000 to every adult American if the GOP retains its narrow majorities in the House and the Senate.

Skeptics roll their eyes at the proposal, noting that previous Trump promises about checks purportedly garnered from tariff revenue and Department of Government Efficiency savings failed to materialize.

Trump’s promise would also become moot if Democrats merely win a majority in the House. The consensus among political insiders in both parties is that they are highly likely to do so.

Nevertheless, voters can “count on it” that the checks would arrive if the GOP pulled off a double-victory, Trump promised the crowd in San Antonio.

Democrats don’t see the Trump tactic as either serious or effective.

“In some places it might matter, but in most places it won’t,” Democratic strategist Hank Sheinkopf told this column. “In places where Republicans should do well, they’re being clobbered right now. It would take a lot of checks for people to change their minds.”

Sheinkopf also noted that Trump has been making the promise often since he first unveiled the idea at the GOP midterm convention in Dallas a month ago. Many opinion polls have grown bleaker for Republicans during that time.

“People know they are [supposedly] getting the checks, and it hasn’t moved their votes back into the Republican column,” Sheinkopf noted.

Still, the $5,000 check proposal is just one arrow in a quiver of giveaways Trump and the GOP are surely hoping will make voters more receptive to their candidates.

A plan is already in motion sending $90 payments to more than 20 million people enrolled in Medicare Part B . In a separate move, almost 1 million people are receiving $500 checks, purportedly because they were overcharged under the terms of the Affordable Care Act (ACA).

There is a whole separate debate about the use of public money in a different way: to fund a series of Trump-centric TV ads. Amid public backlash, Trump on Monday promised future ads would be paid for by him or his main super PAC.

But the White House has ruled out reimbursements for money already spent on the ads — which The New York Times estimated as more than $11 million. The Democratic National Committee is suing over the matter.

Trump has vigorously defended the payments related to Medicare and the ACA.

Announcing the $90 Medicare-related payments in a social media post late last week, Trump wrote that the money was intended “to help pay for [recipients’] Medicare Part B premiums, which we have already reduced by significant amounts.”

He added that the money would come from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which he derided as “a pointless ‘Slush Fund.’”

A separate fact sheet from the White House said the fund “has been given $2 billion by Congress for the purposes of making improvements to the Medicare fee-for-service program, but has never before been utilized.”

As for the $500 payments relating to the Affordable Care Act, mailed checks are to be accompanied by a letter from Trump.

A copy of the letter seen by The Hill stated: “For years, the Biden Administration overcharged you to fund the operation of HealthCare.gov. That money belongs to hard-working Americans, not the Government, and now I am returning it to you!”

The White House has pushed back against questions about the ethics of these actions, or whether they amount to electioneering.

A spokesperson recently asserted to NPR that such lines of attack were “out-of-touch criticism.”

Some ethics experts emphasize that not all of Trump’s efforts are quite the same.

Richard Painter, who served as the chief White House ethics lawyer during former President George W. Bush’s administration, asserted that the taxpayer-funded Trump-centric TV ads “definitely crossed the line. Those were illegal. Those were propaganda.”

But Painter also characterized the pledge of the $5,000 checks in the event of a GOP midterm victory as “a stupid promise” rather than an illegal one — even as he doubted that the president could get such a windfall authorized by Congress.

And he seemed even more relaxed about the Medicare and ACA-related payments.

“Big announcements right before Election Day are par for the course in politics,” he said. “Politicians love to tax you in April and spend your money in October and November.”

But others take a far more critical view.

“Within weeks of the election that could cost him Congress, based on recent polling, he is suggesting monies are available now to certain categories of U.S. persons,” said Virginia Canter, chief counsel for ethics and anti-corruption at the Democracy Defenders Fund.

Canter, who served as a White House associate counsel for former Presidents Clinton and Obama, added: “It basically suggests [the monies] are aimed at influencing the voting in favor of Republican candidates.”

Canter also claimed the payments appeared highly questionable legally, given the traditional power of Congress over spending.

“When Congress does enact legislation, it’s for specific purposes and any payments have to be for the purposes for which they’ve been appropriated,” she said. “It’s not in the hands of the president.”

Trump, predictably, seems unbothered by all that.

Reiterating his promise about the $5,000 checks in a video earlier this week, he boasted about his economic record.

“Our country is doing so well under Republican leadership that only I can make you this promise,” he insisted.

The Memo is a reported column by Niall Stanage.
